sentences.text: Training for the Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System shall be completed before each fire season and refreshed whenever operating procedures or field configurations change.
The training program shall be role based so that each participant practices the decisions, system functions, communications, and safety constraints that apply to the assigned position.

The Duty Detection Officer shall be trained to operate the Caldera Incident Command Portal, review detections, validate confidence indicators, and escalate suspected ignitions according to the approved incident workflow.

Camera familiarization shall cover the North Lookout Camera Mast and the South Lookout Camera Mast, including normal image behavior, degraded visibility conditions, routine inspection cues, and reporting of equipment faults.

The Duty Detection Officer shall also learn how the Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine and the Smoke Classifier Module present uncertainty so that human confirmation remains part of every operational decision.
The Drone Pilot Operator shall be trained on Horizon Ridge Drone Dock procedures, Drone Tasking Service mission controls, safe launch checks, recovery actions, and loss-of-link coordination.

The Air Attack Supervisor shall be trained to interpret system status during aerial operations and to coordinate with the Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console without bypassing airspace safety requirements.

The Tanker Base Manager shall receive practical instruction on status entry, loading coordination, and abnormal-condition reporting for the East Retardant Loading Pump and the West Retardant Loading Pump.
The Helitack Crew Leader shall be trained on use of the Crewline Mobile Tablet, field acknowledgments, location updates, and communication discipline during changing fire behavior.
During field mobilization drills, the Helitack Crew Leader shall use the staging pin to confirm that the assigned crew is positioned at the exercise location.
The County Emergency Liaison shall be trained to interpret public-safety information from the Caldera Incident Command Portal and to coordinate notifications with county procedures.
All operational users shall receive communications training that includes VHF Radio Gateway Repeater failure modes, alternate contact paths, call signs, message brevity, and confirmation readbacks.

Weather training shall explain how the MesoWest Weather Fusion Node supports situational awareness and how operators should treat weather inputs when local observations conflict with displayed values.
Initial qualification shall include supervised console practice, scenario walkthroughs, and a documented check by an instructor who is authorized by the operations lead.
Annual refresher training shall include changes to software screens, revised thresholds, updated contact rosters, seasonal hazard briefings, and lessons learned from prior incidents.

Tabletop exercises shall be conducted before the expected peak fire period and shall test detection triage, command notification, airspace coordination, tanker-base coordination, crew deployment, and public-agency liaison actions.
Live exercises shall be scheduled at least once per season when conditions permit and shall include field crews, aircraft coordination staff, drone operations staff, and command-center personnel.

Exercise controllers shall inject realistic complications such as intermittent network service, obscured camera views, delayed field confirmation, resource conflicts, and conflicting reports from external observers.

Performance measures shall include time from automated detection to human review, time from review to command notification, time to resource assignment, communication completion rate, and accuracy of incident status updates.

Detection quality shall be evaluated using confirmed events, benign smoke sources, weather-related artifacts, and operator notes so that both missed detections and false alarms are visible to program management.
Every false-alarm review shall identify the apparent cause, affected sensors or analytic outputs, operator actions, dispatch consequences, and any recommended tuning or training change.
The review board shall include operations, aviation, field crew, maintenance, and county liaison representatives when the event affected more than one operational function.

Seasonal readiness shall require each active user to demonstrate current proficiency, complete required safety briefings, and acknowledge the current operating procedures before receiving operational access.

Personnel who do not meet proficiency requirements shall complete remedial training and a repeat evaluation before performing unsupervised duties in the Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System.
